item.title: Nunobiki Falls: Four Waterfalls Minutes from Central Kobe — Guide
item.description: Nunobiki Falls is one of the most remarkable things about Kobe: a chain of four waterfalls, celebrated in classical Japanese poetry for over a thousand years and counted among the country’s finest, sitting barely fifteen minutes' walk from a Shinkansen station. A shaded stone path climbs from behind Shin-Kobe Station past the Mendaki, Ondaki, Tsuzumigadaki and Meotodaki falls, the largest dropping some 43 metres into a green pool. Keep climbing and the trail reaches a viewing plaza over the city, the Nunobiki Herb Garden and a ropeway back down.
